site_description: An ADHD-friendly chore and task companion that lives inside Home Assistant.

landing.hero_line_2: A pet that cheers you on.
landing.lead: Boopli is an ADHD-friendly chore companion that lives inside Home Assistant. It nudges you with the lights, speakers and phone you already have. No account and no server. Nothing is sent anywhere unless you turn on AI help. Available in English, German, Dutch, French and Spanish.
landing.badge_hacs_alt: Open your Home Assistant instance and open this repository in HACS.
landing.badge_setup_alt: Open your Home Assistant instance and start setting up Boopli.
landing.early_note: Early development: Boopli is not ready for daily use yet. Free and open source (MIT).
landing.hero_image_alt: Boopli the slime in its room, next to a water bowl, a food bowl and a bed
landing.steps_title: Up and running in three steps
landing.step_1: Add it. Add the repository to HACS and download Boopli.
landing.step_2: Switch it on. Add the Boopli integration under Settings, Devices & services.
landing.step_3: Follow the wizard. Open Boopli in the sidebar. A guide asks one question per screen.
landing.feature_1_title: Tiny steps, one at a time
landing.feature_1_text: A big chore becomes a few very small steps. Boopli shows only the one that is your turn, with a big Done button. Steps can wait for a sensor, an NFC tag or a button, and finish by themselves.
landing.feature_2_text: A light blinks. A speaker dings, then speaks. A siren sounds if you really need it. Build your own nudge sequences, per chore, and let your phone join in. Quiet hours and away mode keep it calm.
landing.feature_3_text: Say "clean my room" and your own Home Assistant AI agent (or your own Claude, as an extra) asks a few questions and splits it into tiny steps that fit your home. Photos help it see what is out of place.
landing.feature_4_title: A wall board for the tablet
landing.feature_4_text: A screen on the wall with the current step, the clock, the weather and your pet. Move and resize the tiles right on the wall, like a Home Assistant dashboard.
landing.what_is_next_note: Straight from the project's GitHub issues, so it is always current.
